key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC delivered the best oxidation protection for SA516 boiler steel, cutting maximum weight gain by 95.71% versus bare steel.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that Ni-based ceramic composite coatings, especially HVOF-applied TiC-reinforced layers, can greatly improve high-temperature durability of boiler steels in oxidizing service.
method: Compared Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings.
Applied coatings by HVOF and plasma spray on SA516 steel.
Evaluated cyclic oxidation at 900°C for 50 cycles using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: After 50 oxidation cycles at 900°C, the HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating showed the lowest weight gain and the most protective oxide scale, while uncoated steel suffered severe spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated in a controlled laboratory oxidation test, so long-term behavior under real boiler cycling, erosion, or thermal shock still needs validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
